meta.rule: Nothing here is a fact about the property. Each setting is either a number published by an official source (the fact id is given) or a range the model sweeps. The property's own rent, expiry date and lease terms are blank, so the model works per $100 of current yearly rent.

settings.label: Rent
settings.setting: $100 a year (an index, not a value)
settings.why: The rent is private. Every result is per $100 of current yearly rent and scales directly.

settings.label: Lease expiry
settings.why: The brief gives a window, not a date. Years of rent left are counted from the end of 2026.

settings.label: Rent increases before expiry
settings.setting: 0% a year in the base case; 2% as a sensitivity
settings.why: The lease clause is blank. The tenant says its leases are generally fixed with cost-of-living adjustments.

settings.label: What the money would earn if the property were sold
settings.why: The Treasury yield is the return with no property risk. The two higher figures are what large landlords earn on purchases.

settings.label: Yield a buyer wants on a freshly renewed lease
settings.setting: 7.3% in the base case; 6.5% and 7.8% as sensitivities
settings.why: The range of purchase and sale yields in the two landlords' latest quarterly filings. No official figure exists for Los Angeles.

settings.label: Chance the lease is renewed or re-let at expiry
settings.setting: 76.2% in the base case; swept from 0% to 100%
settings.why: Share of Realty Income's expiring leases renewed by the same tenant in the nine months to September 30, 2026. A portfolio average, not a forecast for this tenant.

settings.label: New rent on renewal, as a share of the old rent
settings.setting: 103.1% in the base case; 103.5% as a sensitivity
settings.why: Realty Income's rent recapture on re-leased properties.

settings.label: Price of the property if left vacant, as a share of its leased price
settings.setting: 63% in the base case; 86% as a sensitivity
settings.why: Price per square foot of vacant against leased properties sold by NNN REIT. A national average. Land in central Los Angeles may be worth more or less; an appraisal decides.

settings.label: Tax rate on the gain, for the tax tables only
settings.setting: 37.1% (the top federal and California rates added together)
settings.why: An upper bound. The owner's actual rate, basis and depreciation are private.

settings.label: Share of the sale price that is taxable gain
settings.why: The owner's tax basis is private.

settings.label: Selling costs other than transfer tax
settings.why: Brokerage, escrow and legal fees have no official source. They make every sale result slightly worse than shown.

settings.label: Simulation
settings.why: Each trial draws the renewal outcome, the renewal rent, the vacant price and the buyer's yield from the official ranges above. Same seed, same result.

settings.label: Stress tests
settings.setting: Tenant leaves; yields 2 points higher; rent stops 2 years early
settings.why: Shocks chosen to show the size of a bad outcome. They are not forecasts and carry no probability.
